topic: Wireframing, Information Architecture, and User Flows
learningObjectives: Organize content using basic information architecture principles.
Create low-fidelity wireframes for application screens.
Design user flows that connect tasks and screens logically.

activities.title: Information Architecture Map
activities.instruction: Explore how an application can organize content and navigation.

content.concept: Information architecture structures content, features, and navigation so users can understand where they are and find what they need.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Provides an entry point and overview of the application.
Groups related products or resources into a browsable section.
Contains detailed information and actions for one selected item.
Provides access to user-specific information and actions.
Contains preferences and configuration options for the user.

activities.title: Wireframe Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the main structural regions of a low-fidelity wireframe.

content.concept: Wireframes communicate layout, hierarchy, navigation, and functionality before detailed visual styling is applied.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Provides navigation between major sections or screens.
Clearly identifies the purpose of the current screen.
Contains the main information or controls required for the task.
Represents the main action the user is expected to perform.
Contains supporting links, information, or secondary navigation.

activities.title: User Flow Sequencer
activities.instruction: Arrange the screens for a typical online purchase flow.

content.concept: A user flow represents the sequence of screens and actions a user follows to accomplish a specific goal.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Wireframe Builder
activities.instruction: Compose a low-fidelity application screen from structural blocks.

content.concept: Low-fidelity wireframes focus on structure and functionality rather than colors, imagery, typography details, or polished visual decoration.
